filament.name: Bambu PLA Basic Orange + Bambu PLA Glow

datums.A: Base bottom (primary). Print bed for the stand.

fits_mm.running_rollers: +0.40 diametral PLA-on-PLA for parts printed separately and assembled (rollers on both races). Slicer XY hole compensation stays 0.
fits_mm.pip_cage_pockets: +0.80 diametral (2 nozzles) for same-plate PIP. Assembled running +0.40 is 0.20/side and welds if the roller and cage print in the same layer.
fits_mm.friction_square_drive_and_cage: +0.16 diametral — tap-in locate of the axle on the square post and of the hub on the bushing OD. Not a press. Functional land starts above a 0.80 mm bed lead-in. The hub must NOT friction-fit the rollers.
fits_mm.thrust_land: Axle sits on the base (stator). Hub sits on the bushing shoulder (they spin together). 0.20 axial float at running lands (flange↔bushing/cage, hub↔retainer). Retainer is a washer that covers the open raceway (OD between outer-race ID and hub OD).
fits_mm.do_not_nest_bushing_pip: Do not print the bushing around the PIP rollers. Race-to-roller at +0.40 is 0.10 mm/side — they fuse. Bushing is a separate body; cage+rollers are the PIP cluster. Axial capture is the axle flange + retainer, not a top lip (that kills PIP).

lessons.title: Start from a blank document
lessons.teach: cad_new_project first. solid_scene must show 0 bodies before the first extrude. Do not continue a recovered or older Print Kit Tutor (tan nest, red disc, leftover helix planes). Hide construction planes and finished loft sketches before save so File → Open is the six-part kit, not orange datums.

lessons.title: Fits are per role and material
lessons.teach: Fits are per role *and* per whether the parts share a plate. Assembled running (rollers on races printed as other bodies) is +0.40. Same-plate PIP (cage pockets) is +0.80 — two nozzles — or the first layers weld. Slip +0.28. Friction +0.16 on a land *above* a 0.80 mm bed lead-in; a bed-printed friction hole with no relief will not assemble after elephant foot. Model 0.20 axial float at every running land. Do not nest the bushing around the PIP rollers.

lessons.title: Snug is not a press
lessons.teach: FDM press fits fail from elephant foot. Friction locate is still a modeled gap, and the functional land starts above a 2-nozzle lead-in on every bed-printed bore (hub, bushing ID, axle square, retainer square). Retain with a flange, land, or retainer — not interference. No metal 608s. No inward top lip over PIP rollers.

lessons.title: Individual parts, then an assembly
lessons.teach: Each body that moves is its own component with exactly one occurrence. assembly_create_component already inserts the root instance — do not create a second copy. Link the stator with rigid joints (axle sits on the base; retainer sits on the post). Revolute the bushing and cage on the axle axis, and each roller in its pocket — never a blade-spar face. Rigid-mount the hub on the bushing OD (hub_mount). The hub is not the outer race. Blades stay one printed body with the hub.

lessons.title: Print a roller pack that takes tip moment
lessons.teach: A tall skinny sleeve cannot hold aero loads at the blade tips. Use a short, large-PCD printed roller cartridge (PIP rollers in a cage, +0.80 pockets) inside a distinct outer-race bushing printed as its own body. Do not PIP the rollers inside the bushing at running clearance. The hub friction-mounts on the bushing OD (land above the bed lead-in) and sits on the bushing shoulder. The cage is a spacer; axial capture is the flange + retainer. Size rollers for FDM (min Ø8).

lessons.title: Keep the machine even
lessons.teach: Three helical blades at 120°. Root azimuth 30° so a 60° helix stays balanced. The square post is the stator — the bushing freewheels on the roller pack; the hub mounts on the bushing. An odd one-sided vane is not a turbine.

lessons.title: Blades and hub are one part
lessons.teach: The rotor is a single printed body: hub plus three drafted helical NACAs, open at the tips. Do not tenon three separate wings into a hub. Print the rotor standing on the hub, tips up.

lessons.title: The section is a 2026-appropriate airfoil
lessons.teach: Directionless VAWTs see reversing α. Build a thick symmetric airfoil (t/c 21–24%, blunt TE ≥ 2 nozzles). Cite NACA 0021. Draft the chord (root > tip) so the standing print needs little support.

lessons.title: Scale is a parameter; 1.0 fills an X2D
lessons.teach: Linear dimensions are the X2D-max design (256×256×260, 8 mm margin). spec.scale shrinks the source (exam default 0.4). Feature sizes that would go below printable (roller Ø8, TE 0.8, 4-nozzle walls) are clamped. noBS-CAD has no document-level scale feature yet — the spec parameter is the source of truth.

lessons.title: Print rotational parts lying down
lessons.teach: Never design a tall skinny shaft that needs a tower of support. The axle is a flanged square puck, printed on the flange. Base, bushing, cage, and retainer print flat, each with a 2-nozzle bed lead-in on functional holes. Only the rotor stands up, and its tips are open/drafted. Cage+rollers are the PIP cluster; the bushing is not nested around them.

lessons.title: Helical blades, not a straight fence
lessons.teach: A prismatic extrusion is idle for most of the rev. Loft a closed NACA at ≥2 stations with ≥45° helix. Mid-chord stays on R. Chord stays tangent. Open tips — no end cap.

lessons.title: Ship an assembly drawing
lessons.teach: Create a drawing sheet, auto-layout standard views, and annotate fits, scale, print orientation, and the BOM. A kit without a drawing is not a product.

lessons.title: Publish the design report
lessons.teach: Write the iteration log, airfoil/Re, role-based fits, roller pack, scale vs X2D, finish, BOM, and plastic cost. READY TO PRINT without a costed report is a fail.

lessons.title: Export one laid-out plate
lessons.teach: Wipe Print-Kit-Tutor/ first so leftover five-plate and shaft/hub/wings names are gone. Save the assembled .nbcad, then solid_move_copy parts onto the bed (rotor standing on the hub, others flat) and solid_export_3mf once as 01-kit. Two materials only: PLA Orange (including the bushing) and PLA Glow (rotor). Do not export the assembled nest as the print job.
